subject: Business Models
title: Groupon: The Daily Deal Death Spiral
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Groupon: The Daily Deal Death Spiral.

hook.text: Groupon rejected Google's $6 billion acquisition offer in 2010. It's now worth under $500 million.

buildup.text: Groupon sold daily deals: 50% off local businesses. It kept 50% of the deal revenue as commission.

discovery.text: Groupon attracted bargain hunters, not loyal customers. Businesses got one-time visitors who never paid full price.

twist.text: Local businesses lost money on Groupon deals hoping for repeat customers. Most never broke even on the promotion.

climax.text: Groupon damaged the businesses it claimed to help. When merchants stopped participating, the deal flow dried up.

punchline.text: Rejected $6B. Now under $500M. It trained customers to never pay full price.

quiz.question: Why did local businesses stop using Groupon?
options: Deals attracted one-time bargain hunters who never returned
